diagnosis.overall_diagnosis: The agent's RaR calculation uses the wrong volatility scaling: it multiplied by sqrt(3) using 3-month volatility, yielding results ~sqrt(3)x too large. Expected RaR values are ~1/sqrt(3) of actual (e.g., 7.10/1.732≈4.10, matches expected 4.11). The exposure formula should use the 3-month volatility directly (not annualized and not scaled by sqrt(3)), i.e., Reserves × Z × σ_3m / 100. Also, Step 2 Slovakia gold value (3263.68) must match expected; the gold price basis for Jan-Sep average may need review. The xlsx skill should be augmented with task-specific guidance on the RaR shock formula and the correct volatility horizon handling.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: The xlsx skill provides generic spreadsheet guidance but offers no domain hint about how to construct the 95% one-sided gold price shock. The agent incorrectly applied an extra sqrt(3) scaling to the 3-month volatility when computing Gold valuation exposure, so all downstream RaR values were ~1.732x too large. The skill does not warn that when the volatility is already measured over the shock horizon (3-month σ), the shock = Reserves × Z × σ_3m / 100 — no further time-scaling is needed.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction: Add a short Finance/Risk section (or appendix) to xlsx/SKILL.md clarifying volatility horizon conventions: (1) If σ is computed from monthly log returns over a 3-month window, it is already a 3-month-horizon volatility of monthly returns in %; the 95% one-sided shock on a position is Position × 1.645 × σ_3m / 100 — do NOT additionally multiply by sqrt(3). (2) Annualization multiplies monthly σ by sqrt(12), not sqrt(3). (3) For Reserves-at-Risk style calculations, match the volatility horizon to the stated shock horizon and avoid double-scaling. Also note: when deriving a 2025 'annual' gold price proxy from Jan–Sep monthly prices, compute a simple average of those 9 monthly observations and verify the cell range maps to Jan–Sep 2025 rows exactly.
